justification: Contribution is a tunable policy planner that decides the agent's next dialogue strategy each turn; evidence is lab training with simulated self-play and results on three dialogue applications, not deployed use.
Novelty is ProgVe's self-generated, self-executing verification programs producing the judgement that drives ProgRe; validated in the lab on three instruction-following and mathematical benchmarks.
GoT branches LLM thoughts into a graph and aggregates and selects among candidate continuations; evidence is lab comparison against CoT and ToT on constructed tasks such as sorting.
A2R's claim is converting citation and hallucination assessments into actionable natural-language feedback for iterative revision; validated in the lab on ASQA, ELI5 and QAMPARI.
FDSP injects static-analyser diagnostics so the LLM rewrites vulnerable code, and the revision is the claim; validated on the authors' PythonSecurityEval against prior self-feedback work.
Self-evolving outer loop rewrites the agent's own prompt instructions and in-context examples from critique-synthesis feedback; validated across 45 lab tasks with no practice setting.
Contribution is distilled critic models whose critiques feed a refiner in a critique-refine loop; a lab study whose headline evidence is human raters judging simplified output.

Problem framed as trajectory-level critique missing flawed steps; contribution is step-level self-critique and refinement inside MCTS, validated on WebShop and HotPotQA (runner-up deliberative_search).
CodeTree's claim is tree-structured exploration with ranking, expansion and termination decisions over candidate solutions; validated in the lab on seven code benchmarks including SWE-bench.
Investigates whether self-debugging on self-generated tests actually repairs code and proposes in-execution repair; a lab study over self-contained Python programming problems.
Headline artefact is ECCO, a reproducible benchmark and execution harness for measuring code efficiency, used to compare three loop strategies in the lab rather than to propose one.
PREFER's feedback-reflect-refine loop synthesises new prompts for the next boosting round, changing the agent between episodes; validated on lab task suites against prior prompt methods.
Mirror contributes how reflection feedback is diversified so revision does not stall at one iteration; validated on five reasoning datasets in the lab (runner-up multi_agent_coordination).
ReAd's novelty is a learned advantage function judging whether a proposed action contributes before it is taken, replacing physical verification; lab validation on Overcooked-AI and RoCoBench.
Novelty is the key-condition masking check that decides whether a response is false before correction; lab validation on open-domain QA, arithmetic and commonsense datasets.
CoT-SelfEvolve contributes the chain-of-thought-guided rewrite of code after executor traceback feedback; validated on the DS-1000 dataset in the lab, integration into practice only discussed.
PIT retrains the model itself to improve its own responses via a reformulated RLHF objective, an outer loop over episodes; validated on two real-world datasets and one synthetic set in the lab.
Sherlock is a training framework whose model keeps self-improving on its own trajectories without external supervision; validated across eight lab benchmarks.
Contribution is a hierarchical recurrent architecture that allocates reasoning cycles per input and learns when to halt; evidence is lab measurement of its own non-uniform step allocation.
Measures intrinsic self-correction by injecting synthetic perturbations into chain-of-thought and observing repairs; an empirical audit of one named mechanism run entirely in the lab.
CoSC chains generate-execute-verify-correct stages so the model rewrites its own result; validated on standard mathematical datasets in the lab, no use in practice.
Contribution is a pipeline training small LMs to critique then refine their own solutions, plus the finding that feedback quality bounds it; lab tests on five math and commonsense datasets.
Claims intrinsic self-correction works once temperature and prompt fairness are controlled; evidence is lab experiments deliberately varying those two factors across several LLMs.
Decomposes intrinsic self-correction into detection, localisation and correction and tests it cross-model on GSM8K-Complex with hint conditions varied; a lab audit of one mechanism.
APR spawns and joins parallel child inference threads to explore the solution space, changing the shape of exploration; validated on the Countdown task at matched context, token and latency budgets.
